questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They work as well as a face shield.
They work as well as goggles.
They do not protect your eyes from wind.
They protect you from objects thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle just before hitting it.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they do not have to catch up with the group. More experienced riders can also watch them from behind.

questions.question: In hot weather, should you wear a riding jacket?

options.text: Yes, it helps prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat-related problems.
Yes, but only if it is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They provide safety benefits and help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader at the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the new rider lead.

questions.question: When you stop your motorcycle, which gear should you be in?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to be seen better. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, what headlight should you use?

options.text: Alternate between low and high beam.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When braking your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds over 35 mph.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had the motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can press the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can press the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can press the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more grip. This means you can press the front brake harder.

questions.question: When do you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you
questions.explanation: You need more following distance when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or in heavy traffic. When you can see through the vehicle, you do not need to increase your distance.

questions.question: In good riding conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same spot in the lane.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on what road and traffic conditions require.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, you typically find:

options.text: The safest place for motorcyclists to ride
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcycle

questions.explanation: The center of a lane collects debris and oil drippings from cars. You may also find utility hole covers there.

questions.question: At night, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distance. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to notice if the vehicle stops and to brake safely.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center of the lane.
Move to the left side of the lane.
Move to the right side of the lane.
Not worry about your lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: In crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by drivers failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers fail to properly yield the right-of-way to riders.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Try to move onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on either side increases danger—it can cause a collision or tempt the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before turning.
Lean in the direction you are turning.
Do not drag your feet on the road.
Do not look at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not look at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet on the road because they could catch and make you lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: What footwear is proper for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that are high enough to cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels may catch on things. Tuck in laces so they do not catch on anything.

questions.question: Who should set the pace in a group of riders?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.explanation: The last rider should set the pace for the group. This makes sure no riders are left behind.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a road with good grip, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a road with good grip, you can keep it locked until you stop. You should still be able to steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: If riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works best for two-wheeled motorcycles, but three-wheeled motorcycles are too wide for this. A group of three-wheeled motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.
